Suspension of solid or liquid particles in a gas.
Disorder characterized by loss of taste.

Particle, typically a protein, which the immune system recognizes as foreign.
Mode of transmission of an infectious disease to another person from an infected person who does not develop symptoms.
Proportion of people that contract a disease in a population initially free of the disease, i.e. during a disease outbreak.

Person who is diagnosed as having a disease.

Proportion of people who die of a given disease out of all the confirmed cases.

Aggregation of cases of a disease within a given place and time.

traducoes.FR: utilisation thrapeutique de plasma de convalescents
traducoes.PT: terapia com plasma convalescente, (syn.) tratamento com plasma convalescente

Body's natural response to help clear irritants from the airways.

Double-stranded nucleic acid whose nucleotides consist of a backbone made up by a modified sugar, called deoxyribose, a nitrogenous base, i.e. adenine, guanine, cytosine, and thymine, and a phosphate group.
Method of performing swab tests on people whilst they remain in their vehicles.
Dried residue, approximately  5 m in diameter, which results from the evaporation of droplets coughed or sneezed into the air.

Mode of direct transmission of an infectious disease that occurs when a person is in the proximity of an infected person who has respiratory symptoms, e.g., via coughing, sneezing, breathing, or talking.

Graphical representation of the incidence of a disease or other health-related event plotted over time.
Disease for which there are many more cases than would be expected at a given time in a given population and which can be ascribed to the same cause.
Number of individuals within a population at risk that is required for an epidemic to occur.

traducoes.PT: limite epidmico, (syn.) limiar epidmico, limiar epidmico (pt-PT)

Personal protective equipment that protects the wearer's eyes and face from sprays, splashes, and large-particle droplets, and prevents the spread of respiratory droplets from the wearer to others.
Sequence of DNA that carries the required information for making a specific molecule, typically a protein.

Therapeutic treatment whereby one or more foreign genes are inserted into the genome of an organism by means of a vector, to compensate for abnormal genes or to help the organism produce a protein that can be beneficial for it.
Complete set of DNA of a living organism, including all of its genes.
Gel, foam, or liquid used for handwashing that may or may not contain alcohol.
Action of removing any unwanted substance or microorganism from a person's hands using water or another liquid, with or without soap or other detergents.
Indirect protection from an infectious agent achieved in a population at risk when a sufficiently large proportion of individuals in the population show an acquired immunity to that infectious agent.

Admission and stay of a patient in a hospital for treatment.
Person or animal infected by an infectious agent.
Set of practices that help to maintain health and prevent the spread of diseases.
Reaction of the immune system of an organism to potentially harmful stimuli.

traducoes.PT: sistema imunitrio, (syn.) sistema imunolgico, sistema imune

Disease caused by a pathogen.
Ability of an infectious agent to enter, survive, and multiply in a host.

Hospital facility that provides critical care and life support for acutely ill or injured patients.

Strategy adopted by a public body because of an emergency that requires people to remain in a certain location which they may not leave other than for exceptional reasons.

Administration and delivery of healthcare by professionals.
Personal protective equipment for the hands typically worn by healthcare professionals to protect themselves from exposure to infectious agents or other biological, chemical or physical hazards.
Strategy adopted by a public body to reduce the number of infected people in a given geographical area and limit the impact on the health system of a disease outbreak.
Means by which an infectious agent spreads from one host to another.

Level of health and well-being of an individual.
Inability of two or more organs or organ systems to perform their function.

Sequence of the repeating units of DNA or RNA.

Infectious agent causing a disease.
Gear worn by an individual that provides protection against one or more risks to a person's health and safety.

Method of performing a laboratory test at or near the site of patient care.

Science of protecting and improving the health of people through the organized efforts of society by promoting a healthy lifestyle, preventing injuries, and preventing, detecting and responding to infectious diseases.
Ongoing systematic collection, analysis, and dissemination of health data to help guide public health decision making and action.

Measure taken by an individual in order to avoid contact with other people and thus help to prevent the spread of an infectious disease.

Method of collecting a sample of organic material for diagnostic purposes by inserting a swab into a person's body orifices, e.g. nose, mouth, etc.
